_doc: The weekly scout report: what exists out there that this box is not using. Written by the Claude routine described in docs/models.md and read by src/lib/model-scout.ts. Judgment lives here; facts about which model ids a vendor currently sells are NOT — those are pulled live from each vendor's model-list endpoint at read time, because a list committed to git is out of date the day after it is written. Fit verdicts are likewise computed at read time and never stored here: a verdict depends on what is running and how much disk is free, and both change hourly. They are now computed PER HOST — measured against the machine this console is running on, and against each other host's declared specs in config/hosts/*.json — so a claim in `why` or `notes` that a model does not fit needs to name which machine it means.
_schema: candidates[]: { id, name, kind: local|cloud, capability, why, checkpoint?, provider?, target?, mode?, params?, released?, license?, docs?, paper?, requirement? { vramGb, ramGb, diskGb, basis, estimated }, spec? { paramsB, precision, contextK, kind }, runtimes?, pricing? }. Give `requirement` when the authors published usable numbers; give `spec` otherwise and let estimateFromParams() do the arithmetic with an honest basis string. `runtimes` pins weights to one stack (e.g. ["metal"] for an MLX repo) and MUST be omitted for portable weights, which is most of them — absent means "runs anywhere", and GGUF counts as portable. Verdicts are computed per HOST: name which machine you mean in `why` and `notes`, because BeTenshi (31.8 GB VRAM + 63 GB host RAM) and B5 (one 128 GB unified pool) disagree about a good number of models. upgrades[]: { alias, from, to, why } — a like-for-like repoint of an alias already in ai-router.yaml.
generatedBy: weekly scout, 2026-09-28 — the week nothing was adopted and two boards were re-read. The Open ASR Leaderboard published a new build (25-09-2026) and moved none of the numbers this report tracks; the Open TTS Leaderboard published no new build at all, and the CSVs docs/models.md tells this routine to pull have gone private, so the tables were re-read from the Space's own API instead. Cohere Transcribe is the pick on BeTenshi for the THIRD week running, unactioned while BeTenshi's stt stayed on whisper-large-v3 — now open #38 of 56 on short-form English. Three of this report's own claims are withdrawn below: Cohere is open #2 on the multilingual board and not #1, last week's TTS ranking omitted two clean-licensed models that were on the very build it claimed to have read, and MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize is 1.83 GB on disk, not the 0.91 GB this report printed — that figure was its parameter count.

candidates.name: Cohere Transcribe (03-2026)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 28-09 and byte-for-byte unchanged for the third week: model.safetensors 4,131,862,976 B plus config and tokenizer = 4,134,794,009 B for the whole repo. Against the 2,065,804,048 params HF reports that is exactly 2 bytes/param, so it is a plain bf16 release with no codec or encoder outside the count. VRAM is 4.13 x 1.15 runtime overhead, not measured; host RAM is the server process only. Benchmarks are from the Open ASR Leaderboard build dated 25-09-2026 — english_short_latest.csv at rev d2c5b38, longform_latest.csv at rev 13d1000 (unchanged from the 19-09 build), multilingual_*.csv at rev d2341ed — read off the CSVs, not off this box.

candidates.why: THE PICK FOR BETENSHI, and the one thing on this list most worth doing this week. Third week of saying so, and the only thing that changed is the evidence got stronger: the board published a new build on 25-09 (adding the abr-ai niagara models, Zipformer, and parakeet decoded through fast-asr-gpu) and Cohere, whisper and every other model this report tracks came back identical to three decimals. BeTenshi still serves stt from whisper-large-v3 on :8001 at 5.78 average WER. Cohere remains the ONLY open model that beats it on all three boards rather than trading one for another: short-form English 4.67 vs 5.78, long-form 9.73 vs 11.23 (top open model outright), multilingual 3.84 vs 4.57. Re-checked exhaustively this week against the new build: parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 wins short-form and long-form and then loses multilingual (5.25); canary-qwen-2.5b wins short-form and long-form and is not on the multilingual board at all. 906 RTFx against whisper's 470, for a 4.13 GB download. Its 14 declared languages include ARABIC, which no other candidate here covers and which this box has an evaluation harness for (config/arabic-eval.json, docs/arabic-model-experiment-2026-09-14.md). WHAT DID CHANGE is whisper's position, and not in its favour: the board grew from 52 open-weights rows to 56, so the incumbent is now open #38 of 56 rather than #36 of 52 — the same WER, more models past it. Cohere is open #9 on short-form, which is worth stating plainly: eight open models transcribe short English better, and every one of them either loses multilingual, is missing from long-form, or both. Unremarkable on B5, which has the pool for it and a better incumbent already. The one caveat is unchanged: the repo is `gated: auto`, a click-through rather than an application, so a human clicks it and reads the terms first. apache-2.0, 211,795 downloads in the last 30 days and 3,393,321 all-time.

candidates.name: MOSS-TTS (OpenMOSS)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, read 28-09: model-0000{1,2,3,4}-of-00004.safetensors 4,932,667,368 + 4,915,961,640 + 4,983,069,760 + 2,148,040,304 = 16,979,739,072 B of weights, 16,995,767,208 B for the whole repo. Against the 8,489,841,664 params HF reports that is 2 bytes/param, so it is a bf16 release with no codec outside the count — unusual for a speech model and the reason the footprint is honest here. VRAM is 17.0 x 1.15 runtime overhead, NOT measured, and no quantised build exists on the hub. Benchmarks from the Open TTS Leaderboard build 18-09-2026, re-read 28-09 through the Space's own API because the backing CSVs are no longer public (see the note below).

candidates.why: NEW THIS WEEK, and it exists because last week's TTS ranking missed it — see the correction note below. It is the upgrade to the CLONING VOICE, on either box, and the case is measured rather than argued. Against ResembleAI/chatterbox, which BeTenshi took into service on 18-09 as the `voice` service on :8004: across the nine languages CV3-Eval measures in cloning mode, MOSS-TTS scores 5.34 WER at 70.73 SIM against Chatterbox's 6.64 at 66.40 — and 13.94 RTFx against 0.93, which is the number that decides it. Chatterbox is SLOWER THAN REAL TIME on the board's own hardware; MOSS-TTS is 15x faster than it, so the same job stops being a batch job. On English they are level for plain reading (2.39 WER each), so nothing is lost. 20 declared languages against Chatterbox's 23, but the overlap is what matters: Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Polish, Portuguese, Czech, Danish, Swedish, Hungarian, Greek and Turkish are all declared here, under apache-2.0 rather than MIT-with-four-t3-checkpoints. WHAT THE BOARD DOES NOT SAY: it measures nine languages and Arabic is not one of them, so Arabic here is a declaration, not a measurement — the same caveat that applies to the Chatterbox already installed. THE COST, stated plainly and it is the whole argument against: 17.0 GB. On BETENSHI that needs a swap, not a slot — the vLLM coder alone reserves 22.9 GB of a 31.8 GB card the moment it starts, and 19.5 GB of TTS does not fit beside it; the console will name what to stop. On B5 it is unremarkable in a 128 GB pool, and B5 is where it should go first, because B5's tts is qwen3-tts-1.7b-customvoice, which the board records as NOT a cloning model at all — so this adds a capability that box does not have rather than replacing one it does. Second caveat for B5: the weights are portable bf16 (no `runtimes` pin) but there is no MLX build, and B5 serves speech through MLX-Audio, so this is a new service on both machines rather than a repoint of an existing port. 3,904 downloads in the last 30 days, 1,564,067 all-time — the 30-day figure is small because the model is seven months old, not because nobody uses it.

candidates.name: AuK-Flash (Tencent Hunyuan speech foundation model, distilled)
candidates.params: the Open TTS Leaderboard records 1.53B; HF publishes no count and the repo ships 6.76 GB, so the count is still not the footprint

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 28-09 and unchanged: auk_flash.safetensors 6,122,209,092 B + vae.safetensors 637,322,604 B = 6,759,531,696 B of weights, 6,762,657,045 B for the whole repo. Byte-for-byte the same size as the AuK base repo, which ships the same VAE beside auk_base.safetensors at the identical 6,122,209,092 B. HF publishes NO parameter count for either repo, so estimateFromParams() must not be used on them; the leaderboard's 1.53B against 6.76 GB of weights would be 4.4 bytes/param, so that figure describes one component and not the checkpoint. VRAM is 6.76 x 1.15 runtime overhead, not measured. Host RAM is the server process only: at 6.76 GB the weight set fits on BeTenshi's card outright, so unlike the image models it needs no CPU offload and holds no standing host-RAM copy.

candidates.why: STILL THE ENGLISH-AND-CHINESE CLONING PICK, and now it has to share the entry with MOSS-TTS above, which is the honest outcome of ranking both on the same board. On CV3-Eval English cloning AuK-Flash holds the speaker-similarity crown among clean-licensed models at 72.67 SIM (AuK base 73.00) against MOSS-TTS's 63.56 and the running Chatterbox service's 53.13 — +9.1 and +19.5 points on the one axis a cloning service exists for. MOSS-TTS takes the error rate on the same test (2.99 WER against 3.35) and all the breadth. So the split is clean: if the job is making one English or Chinese voice sound like a specific person, this is the model and it is a third the download; if the job is many languages, MOSS-TTS is. On Seed-TTS English cloning the similarity gap repeats: AuK-Flash 0.80 WER / 75.71 SIM against ChatterboxTTS 1.07 / 59.51. Flash over the base checkpoint for the same 6.76 GB, trading 0.11 WER for 4-6x the throughput (26.61 vs 4.28 RTFx on CV3, 18.55 vs 4.47 on Seed-TTS). THE COSTS, unchanged: zh and en only, where Chatterbox declares 23 languages, and neither board measures Arabic at all; AuK is an instruction-driven pipeline that also does speech editing, enhancement and source separation, which nothing on either box can do, so it is a new service to write rather than a repoint of :8004. NEW FACT THIS WEEK, and it makes the case for some cloning upgrade stronger than it was: config/hosts/betenshi.json, updated 22-09, records that local-chatterbox returns HTTP 500 for its own built-in voice and names KOKORO as BeTenshi's declared tts driver. The cloning voice that shipped on 18-09 is not actually serving on that box. On BeTenshi 6.76 GB sits on the card beside Kokoro and Chatterbox without disturbing them; unremarkable on B5. Adoption is almost nil and should be said rather than hidden: 2,957 downloads in the last 30 days, 2,979 all-time.

candidates.name: Qwen3-TTS 12Hz (1.7B CustomVoice)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 28-09 and unchanged: model.safetensors 3,833,402,552 B (= 1,916,676,352 params x 2 bytes, so bf16) PLUS speech_tokenizer/model.safetensors 682,293,092 B, which the 1.7B in the name does not include — 4,520,218,951 B for the whole repo. VRAM is that x 1.15 runtime overhead. Not measured. Ignore the repo's `usedStorage` of 4,604,822,661 B; it counts revisions the download does not fetch.

candidates.why: IN SERVICE ON B5 since 20-09, so this speaks only to BETENSHI, where it remains the answer to one narrow question: reading non-English text aloud. Across all nine languages CV3-Eval measures it ranks 3rd at 4.22 average WER; Kokoro is unranked because it has no German, Korean or Russian at all, and the multilingual voice BeTenshi gained on 18-09 — Chatterbox — ranks 10th at 11.28. Per language, reading without cloning: German 5.96 against Chatterbox's 17.45, French 5.94 against 16.34, Russian 5.70 against 13.49, Japanese 5.90 against 8.82. Nothing here should repoint :8002: on English Kokoro-82M scores 1.46 WER at 69.0 RTFx against this one's 1.71 at 13.32, with 103.9 ms time-to-first-audio against 309.9 — faster, more intelligible and a fortieth of the size, exactly as last week's correction said. ONE THING HAS CHANGED, and it is a rival rather than a reversal: FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512 (RL) was on the same board last week and this report failed to mention it. On the eight languages where both are measured and neither is broken it averages 3.62 against this model's 4.01, at 1.68 English WER — better, cheaper on paper, and it collapses on Japanese (43.88 CER against 5.90) and starts talking a full second late (1058.7 ms TTFA). So Qwen3-TTS keeps this slot on Japanese and latency, not on breadth alone, and the honest summary is that the gap to the alternative is smaller than this entry implied. Still not a cloning model: the board records CustomVoice as no-cloning, the `-Base` sibling is the cloning variant and ranks 3rd in cloning mode at 72.60 SIM. Downloads by metric: 2,408,453 in the last 30 days (down from 2.57M), 15,664,163 all-time (up from 15.17M) — still the most-pulled clean-licensed TTS this month, narrowly, at 1.4x Chatterbox's 1,711,416.

candidates.name: Qwen3-ASR 1.7B (transformers build)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 28-09 and byte-for-byte unchanged: model.safetensors 4,076,193,080 B plus tokenizer and config = 4,087,646,324 B for the whole repo. That file size divided by the 2,038,052,480 params HF reports is exactly 2 bytes/param, so the release is bf16 and there is no hidden encoder or codec outside the count. VRAM is 4.09 x 1.15 runtime overhead, not measured; host RAM is the server process only. B5 runs an 8-bit MLX build instead, which is roughly half this on disk — that figure has not been read off B5 and is not claimed here.

candidates.why: IN SERVICE ON B5 since 20-09 as qwen3-asr-1.7b-8bit, so this speaks only to BETENSHI, where :8001 is still whisper-large-v3. It keeps its place for one narrow reason and loses on everything else, and the 25-09 build changed neither half. It is open #1 on short-form English — 4.31 average WER against whisper's 5.78, a 25% relative error reduction, at 820 RTFx against 470 — and 10th overall, with every model above it proprietary. On the multilingual board it averages 5.53 against whisper's 4.57: WORSE than the model it would replace on every one of the six measured European languages except German and Spanish, despite the 30 languages its own metadata advertises and the 52 the board credits it with. It is absent from the long-form board entirely, so nothing is known about how it handles a meeting recording rather than a clean utterance. Cohere above beats it on two boards of three and loses the third by 0.36, which is why Cohere is the pick and this is the specialist: take it on BeTenshi only if that box transcribes short English audio and nothing else, which is what voice input in the Studio actually is. Note the cheap sibling that appeared on this build: Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-hf is 5.045 short-form and 9.01 multilingual, so a third the size for worse-than-whisper multilingual — not a substitute. 329,785 downloads in the last 30 days, 608,062 all-time.

candidates.name: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming 1.5B
candidates.params: 2.81B (the '1.5B' in the name is the LLM backbone only)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 28-09 and unchanged: model-0000{1,2,3}-of-00003.safetensors 2,498,354,152 + 2,486,576,066 + 643,458,072 B = 5.63 GB of weights, 5,645,212,528 B for the whole repo. Against the 2,814,116,321 params HF reports that is exactly 2 bytes/param, so it is a bf16 release with no separate codec outside the count. Note the name understates it: '1.5B' is the language backbone, the checkpoint is 2.81B. VRAM is 5.63 x 1.15 runtime overhead, not measured; host RAM is the server process only.

candidates.why: UNMEASURED, and that is still the whole shape of this entry: it is absent from all three Open ASR boards on the 25-09 build as it was on the 19-09 and 11-09 ones, so it has no accuracy number and the ones this report printed for two weeks belonged to microsoft/VibeVoice-ASR-HF, a different 8B checkpoint. What is left needs no benchmark: it is the only MIT-licensed model on this list that streams speaker-attributed transcription as audio arrives, and local-whisper on BeTenshi cannot show live text or tell two speakers apart at all. So install it for live diarised transcription behind its own service, and do not repoint the stt capability at it — the general route belongs to Cohere. IT NOW HAS A RIVAL IN THE SAME UNMEASURED STATE: Edge0/Audio8-ASR-Infinite, apache-2.0, 8.19 GB, streaming and realtime by its own tags, is the #1 trending ASR model on the hub this week at 1,202 likes — and absent from every board, declaring only zh and en against this model's 10. Only the 0.1B member of that family (AutoArk-AI/Audio8-ASR-0.1B, 6.95 WER) is measured at all. Trending is not evidence, so neither model gets promoted on it, and between two unmeasured streamers the smaller one with five times the language coverage and a diarisation story is the one to try. If DIARISATION ALONE is the need, OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize IS measured — 4.64 short-form English at 381 RTFx under Apache-2.0, against a multilingual 9.08, so English-first — and one correction belongs here: this report called it '0.91 GB', which was its PARAMETER COUNT read as gigabytes. The repo is 1,833,165,246 B, so 1.83 GB. Still the better buy than this on every measured axis except the streaming itself. On BeTenshi 5.65 GB sits comfortably beside the speech services; the 7B sibling at 17.36 GB runs alone there and blocks every image model, and is unremarkable on B5 — that is where the 7B goes if its accuracy is wanted. 11,760 downloads all-time.

upgrades.why: Raised 2026-09-07, so TWENTY-ONE DAYS outstanding, read from `git log --follow config/model-scout.json` rather than counted by hand. The price case was re-verified this week against OpenAI's published pricing page and holds exactly: gpt-5.5 is $5.00/$30.00 per 1M input/output tokens, gpt-5.6-terra is $2.00/$12.00 — a 2.5x cut on both sides of the meter, and llm-stats puts them at GPQA 0.936 and 0.929, so the capability is a wash and the money is not. gpt-5.5 is still carried in the pricing table; the urgency is cost, not retirement, as last week's correction established. Terra, not sol or luna: sol is $4.00/$20.00 and luna $0.20/$1.20, so both change what the alias means, and this alias is the stable one applications call. NEW AND WORTH ONE MORE STEP: OpenAI now publishes a gpt-6 family — gpt-6-astra $10.00/$50.00 (GPQA 0.96), gpt-6-sol $2.00/$10.00 and gpt-6-luna $0.10/$0.50, the latter two released 2026-09-22. gpt-6-sol matches terra's input price, undercuts its output by 17%, and is a generation newer — but it has NO benchmark scores on llm-stats yet and, unlike terra, it is NOT wired in ai-router.yaml (only gpt-6-astra is, from the 18-09 wire-all). So: terra is the one-line edit available right now; gpt-6-sol is the better destination and costs a Wire all first. This is still the repoint the console cannot make for you — familyKey() strips version tokens and cannot see that 'terra' is a tier name.

FORTY DAYS outstanding — first raised 2026-08-19, read from `git log --follow config/model-scout.json`, not incremented from last week's 'thirty-three'. THE TARGET HAS MOVED and this entry moves with it: Claude Opus 5.5 shipped 2026-09-22 and Anthropic's own pricing page puts it at $4/$20 per MTok against $5/$25 for both Opus 5 and the wired Opus 4.8 — a 20% cut for the newer model, with a cache-hit multiplier of 0.05x instead of the standard 0.1x, and llm-stats measures its throughput at 163 tok/s against Opus 5's 166, so nothing is given up on speed. Two generations of price-identical Opus have now passed this alias. THE COST OF THE NEW TARGET: claude-opus-5-5 is not yet wired, where claude-opus-5 has been since the 18-08 wire-all, so this is Wire all then repoint rather than a one-line edit. If only one edit is on the table, repoint to claude-opus-5 and take the 5.5 saving next week. Both beat 4-8, which is the point; the tokenizer caveat below does not apply here, since 4-8 and everything above it use the newer tokenizer already.

Forty days outstanding, dated from git. claude-sonnet-5 shipped 2026-06-30; the wired claude-sonnet-4-6 dates from 2026-02-17, which makes this the most stale alias in the file at just over seven months. The parallel `claude-sonnet-5` alias already exists from wire-all, so the repoint is a one-line edit. THE ARGUMENT IS CAPABILITY, NOT PRICE, and the price half of it needs a correction this report has not made before. On paper Sonnet 5 is $2/$10 against 4.6's $3/$15, a 33% per-token cut. But Anthropic's pricing page states that Claude 4.7 and later models use a newer tokenizer producing APPROXIMATELY 30% MORE TOKENS for the same text, and Sonnet 4.6 is on the previous one. Those two numbers very nearly cancel, so nobody should expect this repoint to cut the bill — expect it to be roughly neutral and to buy a better model: SWE-bench Verified 0.852 against 0.796, HLE 0.574 against 0.490. Also note the footnote that the $2/$10 introductory price is now the standard price and the increase to $3/$15 scheduled for 1 September will not happen, so the comparison is stable rather than a promotion about to lapse.

Forty days outstanding, dated from git, and this week it gets a correction and a better target. THE CORRECTION: there is no price argument here, and if any earlier reading of this entry implied one it is withdrawn. llm-stats records gemini-3.6-flash at $1.50/$7.50 and 3.7/3.8-flash at $0.75/$3.75, which reads like a 2x cut; Google's own pricing page puts ALL THREE at $0.75/$3.75 through 31 December 2026, rising to $1.50/$7.50 on 1 January 2027. The leaderboard is carrying the post-2026 price for the older model. So the case is version and throughput only: llm-stats measures 3.7-flash at 207 tok/s against 3.6's 368, which is actually SLOWER, and Google publishes no release dates through its API, so this remains the weakest of the five repoints. THE BETTER TARGET: gemini-3.8-flash shipped 2026-09-02 at the same $0.75/$3.75 and llm-stats measures it at 449 tok/s — faster than either — but it is not wired, so it needs a Wire all first where 3.7-flash is a one-line edit. Not re-checked against the live ListModels endpoint, because this run has no GEMINI_API_KEY. Do NOT repoint at gemini-flash-latest, which is also wired: see the note about pinning.

Forty days outstanding, dated from git, and unchanged in substance. gpt-transcribe appeared 2026-07-27, dropping the 4o generation marker the way gpt-image did; gpt-4o-transcribe dates from 2025-03. It is wired under its own id already, so this is a one-line edit. Audio prices were NOT re-read this week — the pricing page section this run fetched covers text models — so nothing new is claimed about the cost of either side. Note gpt-live-transcribe shipped the same day for streaming, which the router's audio_transcription mode does not front: the VibeVoice and Audio8 candidates above are the local answer to that gap, both unmeasured, and this repoint is the cloud half of the same problem.

The capability that box gained ten days ago is not actually serving, which is why two TTS entries above argue against Chatterbox on measurements rather than treating it as settled.

CORRECTING THIS REPORT IN THE OPEN, first of three. Last week's STT note called Cohere 'open #1' on the multilingual board while the very same report said two paragraphs later that 'Voxtral-Small-24B-2507 is the best open multilingual model after Cohere (3.74)'. Both cannot be true and the second is the correct one: mistralai/Voxtral-Small-24B-2507 averages 3.74 against Cohere's 3.84, so COHERE IS OPEN #2 on that board, not #1. It changes no recommendation — Voxtral is 24B, won't fit BeTenshi and is comfortable on B5 — but a rank is a claim and this one was wrong. Two smaller ones fall out of the same re-read: HojoAI/Hojo-ASR-Multi-V1 (apache-2.0, 11.97 GB, a Qwen3-4B fine-tune) averages 3.54 on the five languages it covers, which beats Cohere on all five — it declares no English and no Dutch, is absent from the English and long-form boards, and has 357 all-time downloads, so it is a specialist and not a pick, but it belongs on the record. And MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize was printed here as '0.91 GB': that is its parameter count in billions. The repo is 1,833,165,246 B — 1.83 GB.

THE TTS BOARD DID NOT MOVE, AND THE WAY TO READ IT HAS. hf-audio/open_tts_leaderboard still serves 18-09-2026 as its latest build — its own version list offers only latest / 18-09-2026 / 14-09-2026 / 08-09-2026, so there was no new build to read this week. THE IMAGE LANE IS STILL EMPTY, and this week it stays empty for a new reason — hardware, not licence. inclusionAI/Ming-Image-0.1-Design landed 17-09 under MIT, which is the first clean licence on a serious text-to-image release in weeks: 6,154,901,056 params, text-rich UI/poster/infographic generation, RGBA output with transparent backgrounds, which nothing installed on either box can do. Then the numbers: the repo ships 52,883,394,518 B — 52.88 GB, because a 33 GB MLLM and a 5 GB connector sit beside a 14.8 GB transformer — and its own card names ONE CUDA GPU WITH 80 GiB VRAM as the validated configuration, served through vLLM-Omni. So it is refused on BeTenshi on size (52.88 GB against a 31.8 GB card, and CPU offload of a 33 GB text stack into 63 GB of host RAM is the flux-schnell mistake again) and refused on B5 on runtime: 52.88 GB fits a 128 GB unified pool comfortably, and vLLM-Omni does not run on Metal, with no MLX port of this architecture. A candidate entry would need `runtimes: ["cuda"]` and would then be refused on both machines, so it belongs here. Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1 is unchanged: `license:other`, 7,115,124,736 params shipping 33.13 GB because the text encoder alone is 17.5 GB, and this week's entire trending text-to-image list is its GGUF repacks and uncensored fine-tunes (one of which, at 964,220 downloads in nine days, now out-trends the original). krea/Krea-2-Turbo and Krea-2-Raw remain gated AND `other`; FLUX.1-dev is `other`; SupraLabs/Supra2-IMG is apache-2.0 and 0.42 GB but is a from-scratch research DiT with 515 downloads and no published evaluation. Nothing in text-to-image this week is both clean-licensed and runnable, let alone better than the Z-Image-Turbo / FLUX.2-klein-4B / HiDream-O1 trio measured on 12 September.

TWO PLACES WHERE llm-stats DISAGREES WITH THE VENDOR and the vendor wins: it prices gemini-3.6-flash at $1.50/$7.50, which is the 2027 price, and gpt-5.6-sol at $5/$30 against the published $4/$20. TWO MACHINES, and this week they disagree about what to do rather than about what fits. Every local candidate above except MOSS-TTS is 4.09 to 6.76 GB of portable weights with no `runtimes` pin, so the fit arithmetic separates nothing; MOSS-TTS at 17.0 GB is the one that does, needing a swap on BeTenshi against the 22.9 GB the vLLM coder reserves and being unremarkable in B5's 128 GB pool. THE RECOMMENDATIONS PER BOX: on BETENSHI, install Cohere Transcribe — third week of asking, and that box's transcription is now open #38 of 56 while its 18-09 cloning voice returns HTTP 500. On B5, MOSS-TTS is the first thing this report has ever had to suggest there, because B5's tts cannot clone a voice at all and the pool makes the size a non-issue; it needs a service outside MLX-Audio, so it is a project rather than a download. The older size asymmetries still hold for anything larger: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming-7B at 17.36 GB runs alone on BeTenshi and blocks every image model; Voxtral-Small-24B, Hojo-ASR-Multi-V1 at 11.97 GB, LLaDA-Image-Turbo-FP8 at 27.58 GB, LLaDA-Image at 49.24 GB, Qwen-Image-2.1 at 33.13 GB and Ming-Image-0.1-Design at 52.88 GB are all refused on BeTenshi and comfortable on B5 — where the last two are then refused on runtime instead.

THE FOLLOW-ON NOBODY HAS DONE YET, unchanged for three weeks and still the single cheapest win on BeTenshi: local-flux-schnell and local-qwen-image are dead weight and both are still in config/model-meta.json. Both were REJECTED by admission control during the 12 September experiment — schnell on its ~28 GB RAM / ~31.7 GB VRAM profile, Qwen-Image on its 28 GB RAM estimate against 28.94 GB available — while Z-Image-Turbo, FLUX.2-klein-4B and HiDream-O1 did the same job at 14-16 GB whole-card. Their weights are still on D: (schnell's stack alone is 31.81 GiB: flux1-schnell 22.15, t5xxl_fp16 9.12, clip_l 0.23, ae 0.31), and removing them frees more disk than every candidate on this list needs to download put together, MOSS-TTS's 17 GB included. This is a decision for a human, not a scout: schnell is the only model here anyone has A/B'd against for two years, so it should be a deliberate keep rather than an accident.

THE PATTERN WORTH REMEMBERING, and the reason this report exists beside the Leaderboard tab: for anything that is not a plain LLM, the parameter count is not the footprint, and the gap is usually a text encoder or a codec sitting outside the count. This week adds the two worst examples yet. FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512 is called 0.5B and ships 9.75 GB — 19x — because the repo carries both the base and RL backbones at 2.02 GB each, a 1.33 GB flow model, a 1.33 GB ONNX decoder and two 0.97 GB copies of the same speech tokenizer. Ming-Image-0.1-Design is '6B' and ships 52.88 GB because the MLLM in front of the diffusion transformer is 33 GB on its own. The counter-example is worth keeping in view: MOSS-TTS is 8.49B and ships 17.00 GB, which is exactly 2 bytes/param, so a speech model CAN be honest about its size. The back catalogue: AuK and AuK-Flash publish no parameter count at all and the board's 1.53B against 6.76 GB would be 4.4 bytes/param; ResembleAI/chatterbox measures 3.0 GB of VRAM and is 13.87 GB on disk because it ships four t3 checkpoints and both .pt and .safetensors copies of s3gen; Qwen-Image-2.1 is '7.12B' and 33.13 GB; LLaDA-Image is '6.54B' and 49.2 GB; FLUX.2-klein-4B is '3.88B' and 23.7 GB; Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B carries a 0.68 GB speech tokenizer the name omits; VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming-1.5B is really 2.81B. Every requirement in this report is built from the repo's actual file byte counts, all re-read on 28-09 and all unchanged from last week.

THIS WEEK'S LEADERBOARD TRAPS, both text. prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf is still the hub's most-downloaded new text model (3,343,748 pulls in twelve days, apache-2.0) and its smallest build is still 5,946,648,928 B — 5.95 GB for a 27B — while precisionLadderFor() bottoms out at GGUF Q2 and would price a 27B near 7-8 GB. The ladder has no ternary rung and should be expected to overstate anything from this family; it is a conservative error, since a 27B fits BeTenshi at Q2 anyway. Note the same family now ships an -mlx-2bit repack, which runtimesFor() will correctly pin to Metal. The week's new giants need no help from this report and get none: XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL is MIT and 1,024,216,603,392 params, MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL is 310B, AikidoSec/altar-1 is 500B and `other`, yandex/AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base is apache-2.0 at 81B — the Leaderboard sizes all of them against the real card and refuses them correctly. XingChen-AGI/Xing4.0-29B-A4B (apache-2.0, 31,215,031,088 params, MoE with ~4B active) is the one to watch there: it is the first model in weeks that the Leaderboard should rank as runnable on BeTenshi at 4-bit, and the KV-cache constant is calibrated for exactly that shape.

Both wired Gemini image models still report the 429 quota error recorded in model-meta.json. That is a billing state on the key, not a model choice — no scouting will fix it. Separately, gemini-pro stays pinned to gemini-3.1-pro-preview on purpose: Google publishes gemini-pro-latest as a moving alias and ai-router.yaml pins explicit versions so an archived result records which model actually produced it. Both -latest aliases are wired under their own names from the wire-all, which is fine; do not repoint a stable alias at one.

Text LLMs are deliberately absent from candidates. The Leaderboard tab ranks every open-weights text model with a published parameter count against the live card automatically, and cloud discovery carries live prices — a hand-written candidate there would go stale beside data that does not. This report's only contributions in the text lane are the alias repoints above, which discovery cannot make because OpenAI's and Anthropic's tier and point-release names look like ordinary tokens to familyKey(), and the traps above, which are the opposite case: models the automatic ranking will size confidently and wrongly.
